messages.subject: repeated rstan crashing R
parts:
I've been experiencing repeated crashing of R while working on stan related things lately - with a fresh R session everything is fine, but often after compiling one or more models and then recompiling a similar model, it crashes. At first I thought it must be related to something complicated I was doing, but even the following simple script leads to a program crash, tested on a windows 7 x64 and windows 10 x64 with R 3.3.0 and 3.3.2, rstan 2.14.1, R term and R studio:

library(rstan)
scode <- "
parameters {
real y[2];
}
model {
y[1] ~ normal(0, 2);
y[2] ~ double_exponential(0, 2);
}
"
fit1 <- stan(model_code = scode, iter = 10, verbose = FALSE)
rm(fit1)
fit1 <- stan(model_code = scode, iter = 10, verbose = FALSE)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: repeated rstan crashing R
parts:
On Wednesday, January 11, 2017 at 6:24:59 PM UTC-5, Charles Driver wrote:
no. but, recompiling seems to be part of the problem I thought - if I don't rm(fit1) then it doesn't recompile / crash, but instead just samples successfully (even though I don't specify auto.write=TRUE , which I always found a little unexpected)
If you don't specify auto_write = TRUE, then it auto-writes to tempdir(), which gets deleted once you close R.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: repeated rstan crashing R
parts:
On Wednesday, January 11, 2017 at 6:40:43 PM UTC-5, Charles Driver wrote:
Is there a way to disable any form of writing, then? Otherwise I guess I can clear my R tempdir after every fit...

No, but I don't think that is the problem. The problem is that the DLL is still in R's table of DLLs and either crashes because it tries to find a DLL that has since been deleted or loads a DLL that is identical to one that it already has or something like that. I haven't been able to try it on Windows yet.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: repeated rstan crashing R
parts:
On Wednesday, January 11, 2017 at 6:40:43 PM UTC-5, Charles Driver wrote:
Is there a way to disable any form of writing, then? Otherwise I guess I can clear my R tempdir after every fit...
Although auto-writing is inevitable, you can avoid auto-reading by passing the output of stanc() or stanc_builder() to the stanc_ret argument of stan_model() and then call sample() on that.
